why: V + C = aV + bC rearranges to (a-1)V + (b-1)C = 0. Give each vowel the weight a-1 and each consonant b-1; a substring is redundant exactly when its weighted sum is 0, i.e. two equal prefix sums, counted with a hash map.
hints: Move everything to one side: the condition is (a-1)*V + (b-1)*C = 0.
That is a sum over the substring's characters with weight a-1 per vowel and b-1 per consonant. Zero-sum substrings correspond to pairs of equal prefix sums.
Running prefix sum plus a hash map of how many times each value has appeared (seeded with 0 -> 1); add the count to the answer at each step. O(n).
pitfalls: Seed the map with prefix 0 so substrings starting at index 0 are counted.
a = 1 and b = 1 make every weight 0: every one of the n(n+1)/2 substrings is redundant.
a and b can be negative; the weights are just integers, no special casing needed.
